## By The Numbers: Sep 6 Performance Breakdown

Let's dive into the data from September 6th. We finished with a 10-5 record, translating to a 66.7% accuracy rate across 15 games. That's a solid performance when you consider the variance inherent in single-day samples. The numbers tell an interesting story about confidence levels and outcomes.

## Confidence Analysis: Where We Hit and Missed

Here's what the data reveals: Our 61% confidence picks went 3-2, while our 60% confidence picks posted a 3-2 record. Interestingly, our 50% toss-up games went 2-0. The 53% Brewers pick was our lowest confidence level, and it missed - exactly what the probability suggested was likely.

## Statistical Deep Dive: What The Numbers Reveal

Look at this stat: Our four 61% confidence picks - our highest conviction plays - went 3-1. That's a 75% hit rate on our most confident calls, which exceeds the implied probability. The Rays-Rangers miss was the outlier in that cohort.

The 60% confidence tier went exactly 3-2, which represents a 60% success rate - perfectly in line with our projected probability. When the model says 60%, and you hit 60%, that's calibration.

Our two 50-50 toss-ups both hit, but with a sample size of 2, that's just variance - not predictive signal.

## Tomorrow's Schedule: Off Day Analysis

No games scheduled for September 7th. This gives us time to recalibrate our models, review the data from today's performance, and prepare for the next slate. Use this off day to analyze trends - that's what the numbers would tell you to do.
